chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Any man who leaves a concubine who has a child, or has a child in her womb, or has no child, if her lord emancipates her, she is emancipated. And if he does not emancipate her until he dies, the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has preceded regarding her, and the Book of Allah is more rightful. If she has a child, and he leaves wealth, it is placed in the share of her child.'

And Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who left a slave girl who had given birth to a daughter from him, and she was small but could distinguish speech. So her mother was emancipated. The guardians of the father of the slave girl disputed regarding her, so he (peace be upon him) validated her emancipation for the mother.

key_terms.أُمّ الْوَلَد: Mother of the child (concubine who bears her master a child)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a slave concubine who bears her master a child upon his death?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the status of the *umm al-walad* (mother of the child), ruling that her emancipation is automatic upon the master's death if not done during his lifetime, a principle derived directly from Quranic precedent. It further clarifies that any estate left by the master is allocated to her child, ensuring her financial security and that of her offspring. The accompanying judicial case highlights the practical application of this ruling, where the emancipation of the mother was upheld despite disputes from her guardians, emphasizing the child's right to her freedom.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyr, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whichever man leaves a concubine having a child for her or a child in her belly, or not having a child for her, so if her lord were to emancipate her, so she is emancipated, and if he does not emancipate her until she dies (so be it), for there has preceded with regards to it a Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, and the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more rightful. So if there was a child for her, and she has left wealth, so it would be made to be in the share of her child’.

And Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> has judged regarding a man who left a slave girl and she had given birth to a daughter from him, and she was small without being able to manifest the speech. So her mother was emancipated. So the guardians of the father of the slave girl disputed with regards to her, so he<sup>asws</sup> allowed her emancipation for the mother’.
